    <div class="mv4-hero-content">
      <span class="mv4-eyebrow-hero">Kalpitiya · Sri Lanka</span>
      <h1>Kitesurfing Holidays<br />in <em>Kalpitiya</em></h1>
      <p class="mv4-hero-lead">A rustic kite camp with wooden bungalows, open-air tropical showers and direct access to the world-class flat-water lagoon of Kalpitiya, Sri Lanka.</p>  
      <div class="mv4-hero-ctas">
        <a href="#mv4-book" class="mv4-btn mv4-btn-gold">Book Your Stay</a>
        <a href="https://www.margarita-village.com/kite-camp-kalpitiya-sri-lanka/" class="mv4-btn mv4-btn-ghost">Explore the Camp</a>
      </div>

  </section>

  <section class="mv4-intro">
    <div class="mv4-intro-inner">

      <div class="mv4-intro-text">
        <span class="mv4-eyebrow" style="color:var(--gold);">Welcome to the camp</span>
        <h2>Your Home for Kitesurfing Holidays in Sri Lanka</h2>
        <p>Margarita Village is the <strong>rustic kite camp accommodation</strong> of <a href="https://www.margaritakiteschool.com" target="_blank" style="color:var(--blue);font-weight:700;">Margarita Kite School</a> — wooden bungalows under coconut trees, open-air tropical showers and a quiet natural setting just <strong>10 minutes from the kite center on Kalpitiya lagoon</strong>.</p>  
        <p>Every morning, guests from the camp walk or hop on a tuk-tuk to the kite center, where the whole community gathers when the wind picks up. Free riders can jump on the boat to cross to the other side of the lagoon; beginners head out with the rescue boat. After sessions, everyone meets back at the kite center bar for sundowners and dinner.</p>  
        <p><strong>Solo travellers, couples and groups</strong> all find their place here. Come for the wind. Stay for the people, the freedom and the most authentic corner of Sri Lanka. <a href="https://www.margarita-village.com/kitesurfing-kalpitiya/" style="color:var(--blue);font-weight:700;">Read our complete kitesurfing holiday guide</a>.</p>  

        <div class="mv4-kite-link-box">
          Want to <strong>learn kitesurf or wingfoil</strong>? <a href="https://www.margarita-village.com/learning/">See all lesson options, prices and what to expect</a> — then book directly with our <a href="https://www.margaritakiteschool.com/kite-school-in-sri-lanka/" target="_blank">IKO certified kite school</a>, 10 minutes from the camp.
        </div>
      </div>

      <span class="mv4-eyebrow">Life at Margarita</span>
      <h2>Good Vibes, Every Night</h2>
      <p>After sessions on the lagoon, the whole crew — guests from the village, the chalets and the dorm — gathers at the <strong>kite center bar and restaurant</strong> for sundowners and a rotating buffet dinner. Sri Lankan rice and curry, tuna BBQ, fresh salads, grilled chicken. Every night a different menu, always good company.</p>  
      <p>Then some nights: bonfires, movie nights under the stars, stories from riders who have just come back from Vella Island or a downwinder to nowhere. <strong>This is the real Kalpitiya experience</strong> — and it starts the moment you arrive.</p>  
      <p><strong>Solo travellers</strong> are the heart of this place. If you are arriving alone, you will not be alone for long. Strangers become your travel family within hours.</p>

        <h2>Kitesurfing in <em>Kalpitiya</em></h2>
        <p>Nearly 7 months of reliable wind per year, warm water and no wetsuit required. Two distinct seasons that together cover the best kiting conditions in Asia.</p>  
        <div class="mv4-season-ctas">

      <div class="mv4-season-cards">
        <div class="mv4-season-card">
          <h3>Summer Season</h3>
          <p>Mid-May to mid-October. Consistent southern winds all day, averaging 18–20 knots with gusts to 30 knots. Perfect for downwinders and kite trips from sunrise to sunset.</p>  
        </div>
        <div class="mv4-season-card">
          <h3>Winter Season</h3>
          <p>Mid-December to mid-March. Wind picks up from noon, 15–25 knots from the north. Mornings are ideal for dolphin watching and yoga before heading out on the lagoon.</p>

        <span class="mv4-eyebrow" style="color:var(--gold);">Find us</span>
        <h2>How to Reach Margarita Village</h2>
        <p>The camp is located right on the Kalpitiya lagoon, just a 10-minute walk from the kite center. Two easy options from Puttalam:</p>  
        <ul class="mv4-transport">
          <li>
            <span class="mv4-transport-num">1</span>
<div class="mv4-transport-body"><strong>By Tuk-Tuk</strong> — The fastest and easiest option. Around 40 minutes, 3,500–4,500 LKR. Find one near the bus station or ask us to arrange it for you.</div>
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="mv4-transport-num">2</span>
<div class="mv4-transport-body"><strong>By Bus</strong> — Budget option. Buses run every 30–60 minutes to Kalpitiya town (around 200 LKR, 1 hour), then a short tuk-tuk to the camp (10–15 min).</div>
          </li>
        </ul>

  <section class="mv4-faq">
    <div class="mv4-faq-inner">
      <div class="mv4-faq-header">
        <span class="mv4-eyebrow" style="color:var(--green);">Your questions answered</span>
        <h2>FAQ About Kalpitiya</h2>
        <p>Everything you need to know before planning your kitesurfing holiday in Kalpitiya, Sri Lanka.</p>  
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          Where exactly is Kalpitiya?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">Kalpitiya is a peninsula on the northwest coast of Sri Lanka, about 3 hours by road from Colombo or Bandaranaike International Airport. It sits on a large shallow lagoon that has made it one of the top kitesurfing destinations in Asia. The area is remote, unspoiled and still well off the mass tourism trail — which is exactly what makes it special.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          When is the best time to visit Kalpitiya?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">Kalpitiya has two wind seasons. The <strong>summer season</strong> runs from mid-May to mid-October with strong, consistent southern winds (18–25 knots, sometimes more). The <strong>winter season</strong> runs from mid-December to mid-March with lighter, reliable winds from the north (15–22 knots). Both are excellent for kitesurfing. Outside of these windows, the wind is less reliable. The summer season is more popular for experienced riders; the winter season is ideal for combining kite sessions with dolphin watching and yoga mornings.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          Do I need to kitesurf to enjoy Kalpitiya?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">Absolutely not. Kalpitiya is a stunning destination in its own right. Guests at Margarita Village come for the yoga, the dolphin watching excursions, the sunsets, the nature and the unique community atmosphere. That said, Kalpitiya is considered one of the best places in the world to learn kitesurfing — conditions are safe, the lagoon is shallow and flat, and our <a href="https://www.margaritakiteschool.com/kite-school-in-sri-lanka/" target="_blank">IKO certified kite school</a> is just 10 minutes from the camp.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          Is Kalpitiya good for beginner kitesurfers?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">Yes — Kalpitiya is widely considered one of the best places in the world to learn kitesurfing. The lagoon is shallow, flat and wide, which means there is plenty of space to practice safely without worrying about waves or strong currents. The wind is consistent enough to make fast progress. Our <a href="https://www.margaritakiteschool.com/kite-school-in-sri-lanka/" target="_blank">kite school in Kalpitiya</a> offers beginner courses with IKO certification and radio helmet coaching so your instructor can guide you in real time while you are in the water.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          Is Kalpitiya safe for solo travellers?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">Very much so. Sri Lanka is generally a safe and welcoming country, and Kalpitiya is a small, tight-knit community. Margarita Village is particularly known for being a great place for solo travellers — the camp atmosphere means you immediately become part of a group of like-minded people from all over the world. Most guests who arrive alone end up extending their stay because of the community.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          Can I see dolphins in Kalpitiya?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">Yes — and it is genuinely spectacular. During the winter season (December to March), mornings are perfect for dolphin watching excursions. The seas around Kalpitiya are home to large pods of spinner dolphins, and whale sightings are also not uncommon. We regularly organise early morning boat trips before the wind picks up on the lagoon.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          How do I get to Kalpitiya from Colombo?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">The most common route is to take the bus or a private transfer from Colombo to Puttalam (around 2.5 hours), and then a tuk-tuk to Kalpitiya (around 40 minutes, 3,500–4,500 LKR). You can also arrange a private car transfer from the airport directly to the camp — ask us when you book and we can help organise it for you.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="mv4-faq-item">
        <button class="mv4-faq-q" onclick="mv4Faq(this)">
          Do I need a wetsuit in Kalpitiya?
          <span class="mv4-faq-icon">+</span>
        </button>
        <div class="mv4-faq-a">No wetsuit is needed in Kalpitiya. The water temperature stays warm year-round. Some riders choose to wear a shorty (short wetsuit) during the winter season when the mornings can be slightly cooler, but it is entirely optional. A rash guard for sun protection is generally more useful than a wetsuit.</div>
      </div>

    </div>
  </section>


  
  <section style="width:100%;background:var(--cream);padding:70px 60px;">
    <div style="max-width:1100px;margin:0 auto;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:60px;align-items:center;">
      <div>
        <span class="mv4-eyebrow" style="color:var(--blue);">Kitesurf & Wingfoil</span>

        <p style="font-size:1.02rem;line-height:1.88;color:var(--muted);margin-bottom:16px;">Every single guest at Margarita Village is either already kitesurfing or thinking about learning. The lagoon is right there. The school is 10 minutes away. The conditions are as good as it gets on the planet.</p> 
        <p style="font-size:1.02rem;line-height:1.88;color:var(--muted);margin-bottom:28px;">Whether you're a total beginner or you're looking to level up — <strong>we've been teaching on this lagoon since 2014.</strong> IKO certified, walkie-talkie coaching, rescue boat every session.</p>
